evidence.claim: World's largest crossed roller bearing and linear motion guide maker; THK-branded crossed roller bearings are in virtually every precision robot joint; also produces ball screws and planetary roller screws used in humanoid linear actuators
evidence.source: THK investor materials; linear motion component market share data

evidence.claim: THK explicitly named humanoid robots as a significant growth driver in 2024 investor presentations; company noted strong order intake from humanoid robot OEMs in Japan and US
evidence.source: THK 2024 investor day materials; earnings call commentary

evidence.claim: Crossed roller bearing manufacturing requires precision grinding of rollers and races to sub-micron tolerances with alternating 90-degree orientation; THK + IKO together control ~60-70% of the global market; 35+ year manufacturing lead on Chinese entrants
evidence.source: Industry market share analysis; precision bearing manufacturing assessment

evidence.claim: Multi-layer exposure: every humanoid joint needs bearings (30-50 per robot); THK also supplies linear motion guides for robot arms and planetary roller screws for linear actuators in legs — 3-4 distinct humanoid component categories
evidence.source: Robotics supply chain BOM analysis; THK product catalog cross-reference

what_could_weaken_view: Schaeffler and NSK gain humanoid share: both have comparable technical capability and are actively targeting robotics; THK's dominance is real but not as extreme as Harmonic Drive's in reducers
Industrial automation downcycle: THK's base business in machine tools and semiconductor equipment is highly cyclical; a global capex downturn compresses base revenue
Chinese bearing makers close the gap faster than expected at the precision tier: NSK's Chinese operations and Schaeffler's Chinese factories already produce some precision bearings domestically
Revenue per robot is lower than reducers: bearings are a smaller BOM fraction than reducers; the financial leverage to humanoid unit growth is real but more modest
